Module building

A co-expression module is a group of proteins whose abundances rise and fall together across biopsies. WGCNA (Langfelder and Horvath 2008) finds them, and each module is then summarised by its eigengene: one number per biopsy that follows the module’s shared pattern. Later steps test eigengenes instead of hundreds of single proteins. Module construction never sees a group label or a phenotype.

Packages

library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(WGCNA)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "workbooks.R"))
disableWGCNAThreads()
inputs <- c(corrected = "01_Processing/03_Blood_Correction/c_data/proteins_corrected.rds")
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))

Input

limpa’s complete matrix with each protein’s blood slope removed from its observed values (03_Blood_Correction). WGCNA takes no covariate and no missing values, so this is the matrix it can use.

corrected <- readRDS(paths[["corrected"]])
abund <- corrected$E
meta <- as_tibble(corrected$targets) |>
  select(sample_id, subject, group, timepoint)
stopifnot(identical(colnames(abund), meta$sample_id))
dim(abund)
[1] 2059   48
count(count(meta, subject, name = "biopsies"), biopsies, name = "people")
# A tibble: 1 × 2
  biopsies people
     <int>  <int>
1        3     16

Define modules on within-person variation

WGCNA treats every biopsy as an independent sample. These 48 biopsies come from 16 people at three time points each, and person identity drives the leading components of the abundance matrix. Left alone, modules would mostly group proteins that differ between people. So the modules are defined on person-centred abundance: each protein’s value minus that person’s mean over their three biopsies.

centred <- t(apply(abund, 1, \(x) x - ave(x, meta$subject)))
expr <- t(centred)
one <- meta$sample_id[meta$subject == meta$subject[1]]
rbind(raw = round(abund[1, one], 2), centred = round(centred[1, one], 2))
        S03_T1 S03_T2 S03_T3
raw      20.97  21.47  20.96
centred  -0.16   0.33  -0.17
dim(expr)
[1]   48 2059

Soft power

WGCNA turns each pair’s correlation into a connection strength by raising it to a power (the soft power): higher powers keep strong links and shrink weak ones. The usual rule takes the lowest power whose network looks scale-free (a few proteins carry many connections, most carry few) by a fit R² of at least 0.85. Here that rule picks a power so high that the network is almost empty, so the power is set by hand:

  • The fit first reaches 0.85 at power 19, where a protein has on average 1.3 connections and 73% of proteins fit no module. Zhang and Horvath (2005) warn that pushing the fit up this way leaves networks with very few connections, too little to find modules in.
  • On pure noise of the same shape (2,059 features, 48 biopsies, person-centred) the fit also climbs with power (R² 0.51 at power 19) while connectivity falls towards zero, so reaching 0.85 at a high power is weak evidence of structure.
  • 12 is the WGCNA FAQ’s power for signed networks with more than 40 samples, the value its author gives when the rule is met only at a higher power (support.bioconductor.org/p/93649, /p/87069, /p/124844).
  • 10 is used here, with modules merged at eigengene correlation 0.75: in the settings screen below this pair gives the modules that best re-form when one person is left out (decisions log, 2026-10-28). The module QC compares powers 8, 12 and 14.

Two settings depart from the package defaults, both recommended in the WGCNA FAQ:

  • a signed network, so proteins that move in opposite directions are not linked;
  • biweight midcorrelation (bicor), a correlation that down-weights outlying values, with maxPOutliers = 0.05 (the default of 1 switches that guard off). pearsonFallback uses an ordinary correlation for a protein with zero spread.
bicor_args <- list(corType = "bicor", maxPOutliers = 0.05, pearsonFallback = "individual")
sft <- pickSoftThreshold(expr,
  powerVector = 1:22, networkType = "signed", corFnc = "bicor",
  corOptions = list(maxPOutliers = 0.05, pearsonFallback = "individual"), verbose = 0
)

Modules

blockwiseModules() builds the network, measures how many neighbours each pair shares (the topological overlap, TOM), clusters proteins on it, and merges modules whose eigengenes correlate above 0.75 (mergeCutHeight = 0.25, the value YvO used). Proteins that fit no module go to grey. Settings that are not package defaults: minModuleSize = 30 and maxBlockSize = 2500, which keeps all 2059 proteins in one block; the settings screen below compares them with finer splits. randomSeed seeds the clustering inside the function; a set.seed() outside it would be overridden. build_at() runs the whole construction, so the QC and the screen repeat it unchanged.

build_at <- function(p, x = expr, deep_split = 2, min_size = 30, merge = 0.25) {
  set_names(do.call(blockwiseModules, c(
    list(x,
      power = p, networkType = "signed", TOMType = "signed", deepSplit = deep_split,
      minModuleSize = min_size, mergeCutHeight = merge, pamStage = TRUE,
      pamRespectsDendro = TRUE, maxBlockSize = 2500, numericLabels = FALSE, randomSeed = 54321,
      verbose = 0
    ),
    bicor_args
  ))$colors, colnames(x))
}
colours <- build_at(power)
sort(table(colours), decreasing = TRUE)
colours
turquoise      blue     brown      grey    yellow     green       red     black 
      340       330       249       229       211       168       167       109 
     pink   magenta    purple 
      104        82        70

At power 10 a protein has on average 19.1 connections and 11% of proteins fit no module.

Module QC: how much the power matters

The same construction at powers 8, 12 and 14, compared with power 10 by WGCNA’s overlapTable(): for each power-10 module, the share of its proteins that land in its best-matching module at the other power. A module that keeps most of its proteins at 8 and 12 does not depend on the exact power.

module_qc <- map(set_names(c(8, 12, 14)), \(p) {
  other <- build_at(p)
  overlap <- overlapTable(colours, other)$countTable
  overlap <- overlap[rownames(overlap) != "grey", colnames(overlap) != "grey", drop = FALSE]
  tibble(
    module = rownames(overlap), n_proteins = as.vector(table(colours)[rownames(overlap)]),
    kept_share = apply(overlap, 1, max) / n_proteins,
    n_modules_other = n_distinct(other[other != "grey"]), grey_other = sum(other == "grey")
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "power_other")
module_qc |>
  summarise(
    modules = first(n_modules_other), grey = first(grey_other),
    median_kept = round(median(kept_share), 2), .by = power_other
  )
# A tibble: 3 × 4
  power_other modules  grey median_kept
  <chr>         <int> <int>       <dbl>
1 8                11   218        0.77
2 12               12   283        0.7 
3 14                9   544        0.7

Settings screen: do modules re-form without one person?

With 16 people, a module that one person’s three biopsies make or break is not a property of muscle. The screen builds each of 32 settings on everyone and 16 more times with one person left out: power 10 or 12, merge height 0.15 or 0.25, deepSplit 2 or 3, minimum size 20 or 30, and all proteins or only those observed in at least 36 of 48 biopsies. A full-data module re-forms in a fold when its best-matching fold module shares at least half its proteins (Jaccard >= 0.5, the YvO rule); its stability is the median of those best matches over the 16 folds. Finer splits (deepSplit 3, minimum 20) re-form less often, so the modules here are kept coarse. A scratch run with uncentred input gave similar trade-offs.

observed <- rowSums(corrected$other$n.observations > 0)
members <- \(colours) split(names(colours), colours)[setdiff(unique(colours), "grey")]
best_jaccard <- function(full, fold) {
  map_dbl(full, \(m) max(map_dbl(fold, \(f) length(intersect(m, f)) / length(union(m, f))), 0))
}
stability_of <- function(p, x = expr, ...) {
  full <- members(build_at(p, x, ...))
  folds <- map(unique(meta$subject), \(s) members(build_at(p, x[meta$subject != s, ], ...)))
  jaccard <- do.call(cbind, map(folds, \(f) best_jaccard(full, f)))
  tibble(
    module = names(full), n_proteins = lengths(full), stability = apply(jaccard, 1, median),
    reform_share = rowMeans(jaccard >= 0.5)
  )
}
screen_grid <- expand_grid(
  proteins = c("all", "observed_36"), power = c(10, 12), merge = c(0.15, 0.25),
  deep_split = 2:3, min_size = c(20, 30)
)
settings_screen <- parallel::mclapply(seq_len(nrow(screen_grid)), \(g) {
  s <- screen_grid[g, ]
  x <- if (s$proteins == "all") expr else expr[, observed >= 36]
  stability_of(s$power, x, deep_split = s$deep_split, min_size = s$min_size, merge = s$merge) |>
    summarise(
      n_modules = n(), share_in_modules = sum(n_proteins) / ncol(x),
      median_stability = median(stability), n_reforming = sum(stability >= 0.5)
    ) |>
    bind_cols(s, n_tested = ncol(x))
}, mc.cores = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1)) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  relocate(proteins, power, merge, deep_split, min_size, n_tested) |>
  mutate(
    chosen = proteins == "all" & power == 10 & merge == 0.25 & deep_split == 2 & min_size == 30
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(median_stability))
stopifnot(sum(settings_screen$chosen) == 1)

Eigengenes and membership

The eigengene is the first principal component of a module’s proteins, scored here on the uncentred matrix so that differences between people, and so between HR and LR, stay testable. moduleEigengenes() flips each eigengene’s sign to follow the module’s average abundance (package default).

me <- moduleEigengenes(t(abund), colors = colours, excludeGrey = TRUE)$eigengenes
rownames(me) <- colnames(abund)
eigengenes <- t(as.matrix(me))
rownames(eigengenes) <- sub("^ME", "", rownames(eigengenes))
dim(eigengenes)
[1] 10 48
round(eigengenes[1:3, 1:4], 3)
      S03_T1 S03_T2 S03_T3 S04_T1
black  0.308 -0.074  0.043  0.013
blue  -0.169 -0.006  0.195  0.050
brown  0.282 -0.027 -0.018 -0.039

A protein’s kME is its correlation with its module’s eigengene: near 1 means it follows the module closely. kME is read on the person-centred data that defined the modules, because on uncentred data the differences between people dilute it. The gene is the first symbol limpa gives the protein.

centred_me <- moduleEigengenes(expr, colors = colours, excludeGrey = TRUE)$eigengenes
kme <- signedKME(expr, centred_me,
  corFnc = "bicor", corOptions = "maxPOutliers = 0.05, pearsonFallback = 'individual'"
)
colnames(kme) <- sub("^kME", "", colnames(kme))
membership <- tibble(
  uniprot_id = names(colours),
  gene = sub(";.*", "", corrected$genes[names(colours), "Genes"]),
  module = unname(colours)
) |>
  mutate(kme = map2_dbl(uniprot_id, module, \(id, m) if (m == "grey") NA_real_ else kme[id, m]))
membership |>
  filter(module != "grey") |>
  slice_max(kme, n = 2, by = module) |>
  arrange(module) |>
  head(6)

How much each eigengene still depends on the person

The intraclass correlation (ICC) is the share of an eigengene’s variance that lies between people rather than between one person’s biopsies, from a mixed model with time point fitted (lme4, eigengene ~ timepoint + (1 | subject)), so time effects do not count as noise.

eigengene_long <- as_tibble(t(eigengenes), rownames = "sample_id") |>
  pivot_longer(-sample_id, names_to = "module", values_to = "eigengene") |>
  left_join(meta, by = "sample_id")
subject_icc <- eigengene_long |>
  summarise(
    icc = {
      v <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(suppressMessages(
        lme4::lmer(eigengene ~ timepoint + (1 | subject))
      )))$vcov
      v[1] / (v[1] + v[2])
    },
    .by = module
  )
module_summary <- count(filter(membership, module != "grey"), module, name = "n_proteins") |>
  left_join(subject_icc, by = "module") |>
  arrange(desc(n_proteins))
module_summary

Validation

stopifnot(
  identical(colnames(eigengenes), meta$sample_id),
  setequal(rownames(eigengenes), setdiff(unique(colours), "grey")),
  all(abs(membership$kme[membership$module != "grey"]) <= 1),
  sum(module_summary$n_proteins) + sum(colours == "grey") == nrow(abund),
  !anyNA(membership$gene)
)

Soft power 10 (signed R² 0.576, mean connectivity 19.1). 10 modules of 70 to 340 proteins; 229 of 2059 proteins fit no module. Module colours are labels only and change if 01_Processing is rebuilt.

Save

modules.rds holds the eigengenes (module by biopsy), the membership with kME, the biopsy table (meta) and the module summary; every module-level step reads it.

out <- here("01_Processing", "06_Module_Building", "c_data")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(
  list(
    eigengenes = eigengenes, membership = membership, meta = meta, module_summary = module_summary
  ),
  file.path(out, "modules.rds"),
  compress = "xz"
)
sheets <- list(
  module_summary = module_summary, membership = membership,
  eigengenes = as_tibble(t(eigengenes), rownames = "sample_id"),
  soft_threshold = fit_indices, module_qc = module_qc, settings_screen = settings_screen,
  module_stability = module_stability
)
holds <- c(
  "Proteins per module and the subject ICC of its eigengene.",
  "Every protein's module and its kME in that module.",
  "Module eigengene per biopsy, scored on uncentred abundance.",
  "pickSoftThreshold fit indices per power; chosen marks the power used (10).",
  "Per power-10 module: share of its proteins kept in its best match at powers 8, 12 and 14.",
  "Per construction setting: modules and their leave-one-person-out stability; chosen marks ours.",
  "Per module used: median best Jaccard over 16 leave-one-person-out refits, share re-forming."
)
write_workbook(sheets, holds, file.path(out, "module_building.xlsx"), inputs, paths)
